commute_time_minutes.source: CSO Census 2022 / NTA National Transport Authority, 2023
commute_time_minutes.note: Among highest in EU; Dublin commuters average 45 minutes; housing crisis pushing workers further from city

working_hours_per_week.note: Above EU average; culture of long hours especially in US multinational offices

vacation_days_taken_per_year.source: Organisation of Working Time Act / WRC, 2024
vacation_days_taken_per_year.note: Legal minimum 20 days; many professional sectors offer 22-25 days

coffee_breaks_per_day.note: Ireland has seen rapid coffee culture growth; 2.4 million cups per day nationally

work_from_home_days_per_week.note: One of EU's highest WFH rates driven by US tech company policies

pub_visit_per_week.note: Pub central to Irish social life; 7,600 pubs in Ireland

gaa_participation_pct.note: % who participate in or attend GAA events; largest amateur sporting organisation in the world

housing.source: CSO Household Budget Survey / RTB Residential Tenancies Board, 2024
housing.note: EUR per month; severe housing crisis drives high costs

education.note: Higher due to university registration fees EUR 3,000/year and private schooling

healthcare_oop.note: Two-tier health system; private vs public; significant GP and hospital costs

savings_rate_pct.note: Elevated post-pandemic caution; housing purchase savings driving high rate

pension_contribution_pct.note: Average employee contribution; Auto-enrollment scheme launching 2025

tourism_spend_per_capita.note: Annual outbound EUR; Irish travel frequently to UK, Europe, USA

diaspora_remittances_received_eur_m.source: World Bank / Central Bank of Ireland, 2024
diaspora_remittances_received_eur_m.note: Inbound remittances from Irish diaspora (70+ million people of Irish descent globally)

uncertainty_avoidance.note: Relatively low; Irish culture comfortable with ambiguity and improvisation

directness_score.source: Meyer, E., The Culture Map / Adapted Hofstede, 2023
directness_score.note: Relatively indirect; Irish communicate through humour, self-deprecation, implication

personal_space_norm_m.source: Proxemics research / NUI Galway Social Psychology, 2022

punctuality_culture.note: Socially late culture; informal settings typically 10-15 mins late acceptable

LGBTQ_acceptance_pct.source: Pew Research Center Global Attitudes Survey, 2023
LGBTQ_acceptance_pct.note: Ireland voted 62% for same-sex marriage in 2015 referendum; major social transformation

happiness_index.note: Ireland ranked 19th globally; declining slightly due to cost of living pressures

craic_cultural_value.note: Craic (fun, good conversation) is a defining national cultural value; social warmth paramount

hierarchy_importance.note: US multinational culture strongly shapes Irish workplaces; flat structures common in tech

formality_level.note: First names standard; casual business attire growing

meeting_starts_on_time_pct.note: Lower than Northern European peers; meetings often start 5-10 mins late

consensus_style.note: Personal relationships and trust key; slow to commit but loyal once committed

corruption_perception_index.note: Score 0-100; Ireland ranked 10th globally; clean business environment

gender_pay_gap_pct.source: CSO / Gender Pay Gap Information Act Reporting, 2024

parental_leave_weeks.note: 26 weeks maternity + 5 weeks paternity expanding; Parent's Leave increasing

us_tech_companies_employment.note: Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon all have EMEA HQ in Ireland; major employer

corporate_tax_rate_pct.note: Famous low corporate tax; raised to 15% for large companies per OECD Pillar 2 (2024)

major_religion_pct.note: Dramatic decline from 91.6% (2006); secular transformation accelerated by Church abuse scandals

atheist_agnostic_pct.note: 'No religion' was 14.5% in 2022 Census; fastest-growing category

weekly_religious_attendance_pct.note: Significant drop; was 81% in 1990; major secularization

religion_impact_daily_life.note: Scale 1-10; declining but still meaningful for older cohorts

secularization_trend.note: Catholic % fell from 84.2% (2011) to 69% (2022) in 11 years

church_tax_system.note: No church tax; donations voluntary; significant Church property/land holdings

religious_holidays_count.note: Includes St. Patrick's Day (March 17), St. Stephen's Day; most have Catholic origin

protestant_other_pct.note: Church of Ireland, Methodist, other Protestant denominations

gaelic_revival_active_speakers.note: Daily Irish speakers outside education system; Gaeltacht areas in west coast

top_platform_1.note: YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok strong; LinkedIn high due to multinational workforce

mobile_payment_adoption_pct.source: BPFI / Banking and Payments Federation Ireland, 2024

remote_work_pct.note: Highest in EU; driven by US tech companies with flexible WFH policies

tech_sector_employment_pct.note: % of total workforce in ICT/tech sector; among EU's highest

startup_hub_ranking.source: Startup Genome Global Startup Ecosystem Report 2024
startup_hub_ranking.note: Dublin ranked globally for startup ecosystem; Enterprise Ireland supports

pisa_score_avg.note: Above OECD average; Ireland consistently strong in reading and science

govt_education_spend_pct_gdp.note: Appears low as % of GDP due to inflated Irish GDP (MNE activity); absolute spend is adequate

vocational_track_pct.source: SOLAS / Further Education and Training Authority, 2024
vocational_track_pct.note: Low vocational track; strong academic emphasis; PLC courses growing

student_loan_prevalence_pct.note: SUSI grants cover many; student contributions EUR 3,000/year are significant

private_school_pct.note: Most secondary schools are Catholic-owned but state-funded; fee-paying minority

childcare_coverage_pct.note: Below EU average; Ireland has highest childcare costs in EU as % of household income

university_tuition_eur.note: Annual student contribution; grants available; government reducing this toward zero

leaving_cert_high_stakes_pct.note: % secondary students sitting Leaving Certificate; points race for university places intense

homeownership_rate_pct.note: Declining from historic 80%+; rental sector growing due to unaffordability

avg_household_size.note: Higher than EU average; multi-generational and shared living rising due to housing costs

avg_rent_1br_city_usd.note: Dublin average; Ireland's housing crisis among EU's most severe

multigenerational_household_pct.note: Higher than EU average; cost-driven in many cases

housing_cost_to_income_ratio.source: CSO / RTB / Eurostat Housing Cost Overburden, 2024
housing_cost_to_income_ratio.note: Dangerously close to EU overburden threshold of 40%; worst in EU for renters

social_housing_pct.note: Very low; major political crisis; Housing for All plan targets increase

housing_price_growth_yoy_pct.note: Prices continue rising despite record building; demand far exceeds supply

avg_age_first_home_purchase.note: Among EU's oldest first-time buyers; housing crisis forcing delay

housing_completions_2023.note: Record completions but government target 40,000/year; population growing faster

eating_out_per_week.source: Restaurants Association of Ireland / Bord Bia, 2023

obesity_rate_pct.note: Above EU average; highest in British Isles cluster

alcohol_consumption_litres_per_capita.source: WHO Global Status Report on Alcohol, 2024
alcohol_consumption_litres_per_capita.note: Above EU average; significant pub culture; Public Health (Alcohol) Act 2018 addressing

coffee_consumption_kg_per_capita.note: Lower than Scandinavian countries; tea traditionally dominant

tea_consumption_kg_per_capita.source: Tea and Herbal Infusions Europe / Bord Bia, 2023
tea_consumption_kg_per_capita.note: Ireland highest per capita tea consumption in world

full_irish_breakfast_cultural_significan.source: Fáilte Ireland / Bord Bia Cultural Report, 2023
full_irish_breakfast_cultural_significan.note: Full Irish breakfast (sausages, bacon, eggs, black pudding, toast) iconic national food

press_freedom_rank.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2024

tax_burden_pct_gdp.note: Appears artificially low due to inflated GDP denominator from multinational activity; actual burden is moderate

housing_crisis_public_concern_pct.note: Housing most cited issue in polling; systemic crisis

emigration_rate_per_1000.note: Historical pattern of emigration; strong diaspora identity

dublin_vs_rural_ireland_income.value: Dublin avg. gross salary EUR 56,800/year vs rest of country EUR 44,200/year
dublin_vs_rural_ireland_income.note: Dublin concentration of US multinationals, financial services, tech drives significant premium

gaeltacht_irish_language_regions.value: Gaeltacht areas (Galway, Donegal, Kerry, Mayo coastlines) ~96,000 people; Irish is first language; special EU status
gaeltacht_irish_language_regions.note: Irish Government pays annual grants for Irish-language media, education; Gaelic revival effort ongoing

midlands_post_agricultural_decline.value: Midlands (Longford, Roscommon, Leitrim) GDP per capita 62% of Dublin; net outmigration; peat industry closure 2023
midlands_post_agricultural_decline.note: Bord na Móna (peat company) transitioning to renewables; Just Transition Fund supporting midlands workers

cork_second_city_culture.value: Cork (pop. 222,000) has distinct identity, dialect, food culture; Rory Gallagher, famous butter market; fastest growing city outside Dublin
cork_second_city_culture.note: Cork has strong sense of regional pride; rivalry with Dublin; Apple, Lilly, Pfizer major employers

border_regions_post_brexit.value: Donegal, Monaghan, Cavan counties face unique challenges post-Brexit; 499km border with Northern Ireland; supply chain complexity
border_regions_post_brexit.note: Northern Ireland Protocol (Windsor Framework) manages goods movement; cross-border communities deeply affected

tech_hub_dublin_silicon_docks.value: Silicon Docks (Dublin 2 Docklands) houses Google, Meta, Airbnb, Twitter/X EMEA HQs; 45,000 tech workers in 2km radius
tech_hub_dublin_silicon_docks.note: Ireland hosts 9 of world's top 10 ICT companies; EUR 47bn in MNC exports annually
